customer.target: Daily public transit commuters who want to sleep or read on train, bus, or subway rides without fear of missing their stop

segments.name: Daily Office Commuter
segments.context: Commutes 45-90 minutes each way on crowded suburban trains or metro lines. Extremely tired on the evening journey.

segments.name: University Student
segments.context: Budget conscious, listens to music or study materials on earphones, travels cross-city daily on metro or bus.

segments.name: Night Shift / Hospital Worker
segments.context: Exhausted after 10-12 hour overnight shift, high risk of sleeping past terminal station into rail yards.

behaviours.name: Daily Nap Habit
behaviours.how: Routinely closes eyes the moment they find a seat; terrified of oversleeping past their interchange station.

behaviours.name: Battery Anxious Rider
behaviours.how: Carries 15-30% battery remaining on the ride home; immediately uninstalls apps that drain >5% battery.

behaviours.name: Price Sensitive / Deal Hunter
behaviours.how: Never pays $5/mo for Western apps like Citymapper; will consider micro-payments under ₹30 if clearly justified.

behaviours.name: Privacy Conscious User
behaviours.how: Refuses apps requiring account login, phone number, or persistent coordinate tracking history.

behaviours.name: One-Hand Multitasker
behaviours.how: Holds overhead rail strap with one hand while browsing news or reading on their phone with the other.

objections: Will this app drain my remaining phone battery on the 60-minute ride home?
Does it fail or lose tracking when the subway goes into underground tunnels?
Will loud ads pop up on my screen while I'm disoriented and trying to shut off the alarm?
What if my phone's aggressive battery saver or Doze mode kills the app in the background?
Why should I pay ₹26 per month if the core alarm is already free?
habits: Wears Bluetooth earphones playing podcasts or lofi music during transit.
Sets static phone alarms that fail whenever the train is delayed by signal halts.
Wakes up every 5 minutes in a panic to check station boards out the train window.
Holds onto grab bars with one hand, operating their smartphone single-thumbed.
Has at least once in their life woken up at the end-of-line terminus station in a panic.

pitch:
# TransitWake

Never miss your train, metro, or bus stop again. Sleep or read in total peace.

TransitWake sounds a high-intensity Cockpit Dark alarm and speaks station callouts into your earphones 4.0 km before your destination.

- **Saves your battery**: Dynamic GPS polling tiers use up to ~78% less battery than standard navigation apps, so your phone won't die on the ride home.
- **Works in subway tunnels**: Subterranean offline caching keeps map tiles and distance calculations running even in cellular deadzones underground.
- **Safety first**: Zero popup ads during alarms. When you wake up, a single tap dismisses or snoozes the siren.
- **Pricing**: The core alarm is 100% free forever. Upgrade to TransitWake Prime for ₹26/month (about $0.31) to completely remove all advertisements. 14-day money-back guarantee, cancel anytime with one tap.
